title: Seattle 2015 minimum-wage step-up: short-run employment effect is contested
body:
Re-read both the Berkeley IRLE study and the UW Evans School study on Seattle's $13 minimum wage phase.
[Step] Comparison
  [Input] IRLE city-level wages vs. UW administrative payroll data
[Step] Findings
  [Output] IRLE: no measurable employment loss; UW: hours fell, total earnings fell
[Step] Interpretation
  [Output] The two papers operationalised 'low-wage worker' differently, which can flip the sign
The headline conclusion depends almost entirely on the unit of measurement (workers vs. hours, single-site vs. multi-site firms). Saying minimum wage 'works' or 'doesn't work' from these papers alone overstates the evidence.
